fact: The Minister of Home Affairs made the Fourteenth Amendment of the Regulations under section 22 of the Identification Act, 1997 (Act No. 68 of 1997), an Act of Parliament, on 23 June 2025, in operation from 1 July 2025, so the Act is in force.
TechCentral reports the National Identification and Registration Bill is only due in parliament in 2027/2028; no date other than the article's publication date is given.

The Department of Transport states that the Identification Act, 1997 (Act No. 68 of 1997) designates Home Affairs as the sole authority maintaining the National Population Register and issuing identification documents, and treats it as current law (document published 2026-10-11, no other date given).

The Citizen reports the Department of Transport saying the Identification Act, 1997 (Act No. 68 of 1997) makes Home Affairs the sole authority to maintain the National Population Register and issue identification documents, and treats it as current law (document published 2026-10-10, no other date given).

Home Affairs' first-quarter performance report to Parliament says it did not submit the National Identification Registration Bill for public comment, as it had to revise it in line with the Digital Identity Policy framework, blaming a failure to appoint a legal drafting provider (reported 2026-10-06; the quarter is not dated in the document).

The Citizen reports Home Affairs gazetted draft amended regulations in terms of the Identification Act, 1997 (Act No. 68 of 1997) for comment until 6 June 2026, with access to identity information regulated under that Act (document published 2026-05-09, no other date given).

The document treats the Identification Act of 1997 as the existing act, with draft amendments to it published for comment until 6 June 2026 (Home Affairs announcement of 5 May 2026); an act of parliament, amended through regulations.
The Minister of Home Affairs replies that under Section 15 of the Identification Act, No. 68 of 1997, anyone aged 16 or over must apply for an identity card.

Home Affairs Minister Leon Schreiber gazetted draft amended regulations in terms of the Identification Act of 1997, open for comment until 6 June 2026, to create the framework for a digital identity system.
Amendments to the South Africa Identification Act were proposed in June 2026, so the Act exists and is being amended for digital ID; the article reports Research ICT Africa's submission on them.
